questions.scenario: It's the Annual School Fest and there's a huge crowd of students. What is your role?

options.text: Standing at the gates, managing the crowd, and ensuring no one breaks the rules.
Sitting at the coupon counter, catching anyone trying to use fake food passes.
Welcoming students from other schools and showing them around politely.
The Head Coordinator, giving orders to volunteers on walkie-talkies.

questions.scenario: You are playing Gully Cricket and an angry uncle comes out because the ball hit his car. What do you do?

options.text: Stand bravely in front of your friends to protect them from his scolding.
Quickly check the car to see if there is an actual dent or if he is exaggerating.
Talk to him extremely respectfully, apologize, and calm his anger down instantly.
Negotiate a deal that you will play on the other side of the street from tomorrow.

questions.scenario: The teacher leaves the classroom for 10 minutes and absolute chaos breaks out. How do you handle it?

options.text: Go to the front and loudly command everyone to go back to their seats.
Silently note down the names of the main troublemakers on the back page of your notebook.
Start an interesting group game like Dumb Charades to naturally quiet them down.
Assign the monitor duties to two people and organize a quiet reading session.

questions.scenario: Someone spreads a totally fake rumor about your best friend in the tuition class. What is your first step?

options.text: Directly confront the person who said it and aggressively demand an apology.
Act like a detective, ask tricky questions, and find the exact source of the rumor.
Talk to everyone individually to clear the misunderstanding and fix your friend's image.
Gather the whole group, state the facts clearly, and put an end to the nonsense permanently.

questions.scenario: You are at a crowded Diwali Mela with your family. What catches your attention?

options.text: Keeping a sharp eye out to protect your younger siblings in the massive crowd.
Doing the math mentally to make sure the shopkeeper isn't overcharging for toys.
Admiring the beautiful traditional clothes, arts, and crafts from different states.
Planning the exact route of which stalls to visit so you cover everything in 2 hours.

questions.scenario: Board exams are approaching. What is your study strategy?

options.text: Drinking black coffee, waking up at 4 AM, and pushing through with sheer willpower.
Analyzing the last 10 years' question papers to find the hidden repeating patterns.
Writing answers with beautiful handwriting, perfect margins, and neat diagrams.
Creating a strict master-timetable for the whole month and following it perfectly.

questions.scenario: You and your cousins are making midnight Maggi secretly without waking up the parents. What is your job?

options.text: Doing the risky physical work like lighting the stove and handling the hot utensils.
Measuring the exact amount of water and masala so it doesn't become soupy.
Serving it beautifully in bowls and keeping everyone entertained while eating.
Giving orders quietly: 'You chop onions, you get the bowls, I will supervise.'

questions.scenario: Mummy is heavily scolding you for something you didn't do. How do you react?

options.text: Stand tall, look her in the eye, and fiercely but respectfully defend yourself.
Stay silent, listen carefully, and gather proof to show her the truth later.
Use sweet words, crack a small joke, and melt her anger away instantly.
Calmly accept the situation, stop the argument, and fix the actual problem.

questions.scenario: You are travelling in a local train, metro, or bus. What do you naturally do?

options.text: Get ready to step in if someone tries to push people or break the line.
Observe people closely, trying to guess what their jobs or secrets are.
Strike up a polite conversation with a stranger or help an uncle with directions.
Look at the crowd and think about how the city's transport system could be improved.

questions.scenario: What is the best compliment a teacher or parent can give you?

options.text: 'You are fearless, brave, and always protect others.'
'You are so sharp, you catch details that everyone else misses.'
'You are so well-spoken, charming, and represent us beautifully.'
'You are a born leader; people naturally listen to your decisions.'

Police_Services_IPS.title: Indian Police Service (IPS) / Law Enforcement
Police_Services_IPS.primary_match_text: You are brave, action-oriented, and have a strong sense of justice. You don't get scared easily and love protecting others and maintaining order.
Police_Services_IPS.day_in_the_life: Leading police forces, solving real-time crimes, maintaining law and order in the city, and ensuring public safety.
Police_Services_IPS.alternative_match_text: If you don't go for Civil Services, your fearless nature makes you a great fit for the Defense Forces (Army/Navy/Air Force) or Criminology.
Police_Services_IPS.roadmap: Take any stream in 11th/12th. Complete your Graduation (BA/B.Sc/B.Tech/B.Com) and clear the UPSC Civil Services Examination (CSE).

Revenue_and_Intelligence_IRS.title: Indian Revenue Service (IRS) / Intelligence (IB)
Revenue_and_Intelligence_IRS.primary_match_text: You have a highly analytical and detective-like brain. You love finding hidden patterns, solving mysteries, and you never miss small details.
Revenue_and_Intelligence_IRS.day_in_the_life: Investigating financial frauds, tracking down illegal money, or working silently in intelligence agencies to gather national secrets.
Revenue_and_Intelligence_IRS.alternative_match_text: Because of your sharp eye for numbers and details, you would also be amazing in Forensic Science, Cyber Security, or Chartered Accountancy (CA).
Revenue_and_Intelligence_IRS.roadmap: Commerce or Science in 11th/12th is helpful but not mandatory. Complete Graduation and clear UPSC CSE or SSC CGL.

Foreign_Services_IFS.title: Indian Foreign Service (IFS) / Diplomat
Foreign_Services_IFS.primary_match_text: You have amazing communication skills, charm, and emotional intelligence. You know how to talk to people and handle tricky situations peacefully.
Foreign_Services_IFS.day_in_the_life: Working in Indian Embassies around the world, meeting foreign leaders, solving international issues, and representing Indian culture globally.
Foreign_Services_IFS.alternative_match_text: If you want a different path, your speaking skills and charm make you a perfect fit for Public Relations (PR), Mass Communication, or Corporate Law.
Foreign_Services_IFS.roadmap: Arts/Humanities (with Political Science) is great in 11th/12th. Complete your Graduation and clear the UPSC CSE.

Administrative_Services_IAS.title: Indian Administrative Service (IAS) / Public Policy
Administrative_Services_IAS.primary_match_text: You are a born leader and a master planner. You naturally take control of situations, make fair decisions, and know how to get work done by a team.
Administrative_Services_IAS.day_in_the_life: Working as a District Magistrate (DM), creating government policies, managing city funds, and solving the biggest problems of the public.
Administrative_Services_IAS.alternative_match_text: Since you are great at managing systems and people, you would also excel as a CEO, Business Manager, or Political Strategist.
Administrative_Services_IAS.roadmap: Take Humanities/Arts or Science in 11th/12th. Complete your Graduation (BA/B.Tech) and clear the UPSC Civil Services Examination (CSE).
